title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts: Recovery by Offset, Intercept and Repayment
content:
Benefit Overpayment Accounts are recovered by benefit offset, by tax refund intercept and by the claimant's voluntary repayments. The Recovery Unit applies the following rules.

## 1. Status conditions

1.1 Recovery by offset or intercept is taken only while the overpayment status is in recovery. The status is read from the Department's overpayment record of the overpayment being recovered, before the offset or intercept is taken.

1.2 A voluntary repayment through an accepted channel is accepted in any status other than paid in full, waived, cancelled and written off, including while recovery is suspended for appeal or waiver review; the card vendor's convenience fee is paid on top and never reduces the balance. The status is read from the overpayment record of the overpayment the repayment is for.

| Overpayment status | Offset or intercept | Voluntary repayment |
|---|---|---|
| Established | Not taken | Accepted |
| In recovery | Taken | Accepted |
| Waiver pending | Not taken | Accepted |
| Suspended | Not taken | Accepted |
| Paid in full, waived, cancelled, written off | Not taken | Not accepted |

## 2. Offsets

An offset withholds the classification's offset share of each weekly payable amount, including payments under other programs and, through the interstate reciprocal arrangement, another state's payments. The offset taken from a payment is the offset share multiplied by the payment's payable amount, rounded to the cent, and never more than the overpayment balance. Offsets continue while a repayment plan is current.

## 3. Application among components

Each recovery is split across components in the classification's application order: non-fraud overpayments carry principal only, and fraud recoveries go to principal first, then penalty, then interest, then fees.

## 4. Excess, closure and employer credit

4.1 A recovery that exceeds the balance is refunded to the claimant when the excess reaches the minimum refund amount, within the refund processing days, as a refund of an excess repayment; a smaller excess stays as a credit on the overpayment.

4.2 When the balance reaches zero the overpayment is paid in full.

4.3 Principal recovered on a chargeable claim is credited back to the charged employers.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A fraud overpayment owes principal USD 100.00, penalty USD 30.00 and interest USD 5.00. A repayment of USD 120.00 is applied USD 100.00 to principal and USD 20.00 to penalty.
- A non-fraud overpayment with a 50 percent offset share and a balance of USD 150.00 meets a weekly payable amount of USD 380.00. Half of USD 380.00 is USD 190.00, more than the balance, so USD 150.00 is offset and the overpayment is paid in full.
- A repayment leaves an excess of USD 0.60 against a minimum refund amount of USD 1.00 (the figure in the payment terms). The excess stays as a credit on the overpayment.
